transcript.content: Hello, it's nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

I... well, I suppose I'm here because of what I've been hearing. I just keep hearing these very clear voices. Mostly in my apartment, but... sometimes if I'm at the museum, in the empty rooms, they're there too. It sounds like... like women whispering from behind the walls. They keep telling me... which photographs belong in the archive. So... that's what brings me in.
Are the voices you hear usually telling you what to do, or are they just present in the background?
I... well, like I just said, they tell me about the photographs. Which ones belong in the archive. So... yes, they are telling me what to do.
Do you believe these voices are real, or do you think they might be something that others wouldn't hear?
I... I'm not really sure. I haven't exactly asked anyone else if they hear them. They just... they sound real to me. That's all I know.
Do you have any beliefs about why these voices are telling you about the photographs, or what might happen if you don’t follow their instructions?

I... I don't really like to talk about them. But... I suppose it's because of the museum board. And the city arts people. 

They... well, I am convinced they've been monitoring my phone. They know that my Caribbean archive will change how the galleries tell the truth. So... that's why it has to be done right. And no one has shown me anything that proves they aren't listening to me.
Have you noticed any times when your mood has been unusually high or low for several days in a row?

I... well, yes. There are days. Sometimes I feel... radiant. Like I've been chosen for this work. It lasts for a while. But... if someone questions my plan, or tells me I need to slow down... I get so angry. Furious, really. It feels like they're trying to erase me. I don't know... it just happens.
Do you believe that the museum board and city arts people are actively trying to stop you, even if there’s no clear proof?

I... yes. I mean, I already told you about the phone. I know they're monitoring it. The museum board, the arts people... they know what my archive means. They know it changes the truth of the galleries. And... well, until someone can actually prove to me that they aren't listening, I have to believe they are. I just... I know what I know.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt extremely down or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?
I... no. Not really. I don't think so. I just... focus on my work.
Have you ever had a time when your mood was so high or you felt so full of energy that it was noticeably different from your usual self, and you didn't need as much sleep?

I... suppose so. Sometimes I only sleep... maybe two or three hours. I wake up before dawn and I feel completely ready. I just... I tell myself sleep is for people who don't have an archive to rescue. That's all.
Have you ever felt so powerful or full of energy that you believed you could do things that others couldn’t, or that you didn’t have to follow normal rules?

I... well, yes. I have days where I just feel... radiant. Like I've been chosen for this. And... if anyone tries to question my plan or tells me to slow down, I just... I get so angry. It feels like they're trying to erase me. I just... I can't stand it.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least one week where you felt so unusually good, so full of energy or so powerful that others might have noticed a big change in you?

I... I think I just said that. Yes. I have those days. I feel radiant, like I'm chosen. And... if people try to stop me or tell me to slow down... I get furious. It's like they're trying to erase me. I don't know what else to say about it.
Do you ever question whether the things you believe about the museum board and the voices might not be true, or do you feel completely certain about them?

I'm certain. I don't question it because... well, it's just what's happening. The museum board, the city arts people... they monitor my phone. They know what I have. My Caribbean archive... it's going to change how the galleries tell the truth. They know that. And... no one has shown me anything to prove they aren't watching me. So, yes. I'm sure.
Have you noticed any recent problems with your ability to carry out your work at the museum or handle your usual daily responsibilities?

I... I suppose things have been difficult lately. I haven't been going to the board meetings. And... well, I missed some bills. My cousin had to get involved... and one of the administrators at the museum. They said I couldn't handle the appointments or the money right now. Or the public events. They just... they stepped in. I guess people don't trust me with it anymore.
Have you ever felt so driven to complete tasks, like organizing the archive, that you were constantly working on them, even to the point of neglecting other parts of your life?

Yes. I... I do work a lot. Sometimes at night, I just... I can't stop. I'll go from labeling the photographs to rewriting the letters for the donors, and then I'm moving the boxes of programs around. I just... I don't sit down. It feels like there's a motor inside me, just running. So I keep working.
Can you recall if there was a time when your mood was elevated or irritable most of the day, nearly every day, for at least a week?

I suppose... yes. There are days when I just feel... radiant. Like I've been chosen. But... if someone questions my plan, or tells me to slow down... I get furious. It just feels like they are trying to erase me. That's... that's how it gets.

Have you ever had a time when your mood was so high or you were so full of energy that it caused problems in your work or relationships—like not sleeping for days, spending money recklessly, or becoming aggressive with others?
I... I don't know. I don't think it was like that. I just... I had things to do. I don't remember causing problems.

inference_history.note: The patient reports clear auditory hallucinations (voices whispering) that are persistent and context-specific (apartment, museum, empty rooms). The content of the hallucinations is thematic (guidance about photographs in the archive), which may suggest a delusional framework. This presentation raises initial suspicion for schizophrenia (F20.0) and other psychotic disorders such as schizoaffective disorder (F23.2), or possibly bipolar disorder with psychotic features (F31.5). Also considering obsessive-compulsive disorder with hallucinations in the context of severe anxiety (F43.22), although the clarity and thematic nature of the hallucinations are more suggestive of a primary psychotic disorder. No evidence yet to rule out other differentials.
Ruled out F43.22 (Adjustment disorder with anxiety) as the symptoms described are more indicative of psychotic or mood disorders with psychotic features rather than an adjustment reaction.
